question: At matched serialized byte ceilings, can a sufficient predictor preserve future endpoint forecasts while a source-linked ledger preserves witnessed historical order and inspection?
scope: Initial native static supplied-law ruler with a sufficient posterior and exact four-probability predictive head. Learned heads, dynamic role changes and query-aware retention remain conditional; this is not an architecture superiority screen.
world: Reuse the declared B04 world-specific static eight-state opportunity/preference/skill endpoint channel, with separately seeded B05 histories. Each history additionally contains observed order and inspection bits independently drawn from fair coins. The input contains these witnessed events; evaluator maker state and future endpoints remain separate.
targets: Four-way future opportunity/artifact prediction and, separately, four-way order/inspection for uniformly queried historical episodes. Report order and inspection accuracy separately. Do not merge future prediction with historical correspondence.

codecs.header: Eight bytes include schema magic, reader kind and record count.
codecs.raw_history: Retain the latest complete 24-byte records: a 16-byte source digest, four-byte episode index and four observed one-byte fields.
codecs.maker_posterior: Eight float64 posterior probabilities plus header, fitted by exact supplied-channel conditioning on all 512 observed endpoints.
codecs.predictive_head: Four float64 future endpoint probabilities plus header; exact readout of the sufficient posterior, not a trained neural head.
codecs.episode_ledger: Retain the latest complete eight-byte records: index plus four observed fields. The source digest reconstructs from the public case ID and index under the common schema.
codecs.predictor_plus_ledger: Full-history posterior plus as many latest eight-byte ledger records as fit.

information_boundary: Shared supplied-law channel, codec and public case ID are external common metadata. Byte comparisons count actual per-maker payload, not application code, transient working memory or an optimal compression bound. Query indices are independent of retention; no truth-dependent record selection. Missing witnesses receive the exact independent uniform prior.
controls: Uninformative channel retains a uniform maker posterior
Endpoint-identical historical twins serialize to the same predictive memory
Independent byte parser and count-likelihood decoder check every forecast
Complete frozen scientific replay before acceptance
analysis: Pair reader differences inside each of eight coefficient worlds; streams, future cases, queries and byte settings are not independent worlds. Report every reader and both targets, exact byte use, retained coverage, separate order/inspection accuracy and shared consumer CPU. No native-to-shift contrast exists in this native-only subset. Every observed episode enters once; there is no copied-evidence multiplication arm.
continuation: Proceed only on the measured cost/quality frontier; preserve the exact counterexample that predictive equivalence need not preserve witnessed history. Do not call a predictive state historical memory when its witness is lost. Independent new-world B06/E04 and remaining fixture categories retain priority after the initial branch.
limitations: Supplied-law miniature â€” architecture untested. No human memory, stable values, learned architecture, original-world headroom, confirmation or new F03 category claim. The raw versus compact ledger comparison includes declared encoding choices.

repair.reason: Pre-dispatch design-schema conflict: B05 storage history used the original-world history field, whose registered grid stops at 64. Renamed the independent memory length to history_episodes; original-world validation unchanged. Frozen memory-1 retained; no PLAN or executed identity created by rejected admission.
